prerequisites: Second year courses of the Common to Industrial Branch module

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to write, sign and develop projects in the field of industrial engineering aimed at the construction, reform, repair, conservation, demolition, manufacturing, installation, assembly or operation of electrical installations.
Ability to direct the activities that are the object of the engineering projects described in the previous section.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity and critical reasoning.
Ability to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Electrical Engineering, both orally and in writing, and to all types of audiences.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert opinions, studies, reports, work plans and other similar tasks.
Ability to manage specifications, regulations and mandatory standards.
Ability to analyze and evaluate the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Ability to apply quality principles and methods.
Ability to organize and plan in the business environment, and other institutions and organizations.
Knowledge, understanding and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technical Engineer.
Honesty, responsibility, ethical commitment and solidarity.
Ability to work in a team.
Knowledge and use of the principles of circuit theory and electrical machines.
Ability to calculate and design low and medium voltage electrical installations.
Carry out, analyze and evaluate projects for electrical power installations inside buildings, whether for business, commercial, industrial or residential use.
Carry out, analyze and evaluate projects for low and medium voltage electrical power distribution installations.
Properly manage electrical energy in an installation in terms of efficiency, continuity and quality.

Perform all types of inspections, measurements and verifications in an existing electrical installation, as well as detect, locate, analyze, evaluate and repair any type of electrical fault or failure in said installation.
Manage information regarding the search and selection of materials to be used in an electrical installation, properly handling manufacturer catalogs, data sheets, regulations and rules.

syllabus_topics: Generalities about the electrical system. Generation, transmission and distribution of electrical energy.
The electrical cable in distribution networks and electrical installations.
Electrical equipment and operation of installations.
Generalities on the electrical system, generation, transmission and distribution
Module 2: Equipment and protection of installations
Different types of low voltage switchgear
Symbolism according to international standard IEC 1082-1
Short-circuit calculation in installations and distribution networks
Protection of people against direct and indirect contacts
Protection of installations against short circuits, overloads and overvoltages
Industrial, Domestic and Special Interior Installations
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, a minimum of 4.0 out of 10 is required for the written exam (E1), 3.0 out of 10 for the laboratory exam (P1), and 4.0 out of 10 for each report (T1, T2). The final grade is calculated as (0.7 * E1) + (0.1 * P1) + (0.2 * (T1 + T2)). A final grade of 5.0 out of 10 is required to pass the subject. For the extraordinary call, similar minimums apply for written (Ex1), practical (Px1), and reports (Tx1, Tx2), with the formula (0.7 * Ex1) + (0.1 * Practical) + (0.2 * (Tx1 + Tx2)). A global note of 5 points is needed to pass; if the global note is 5 or more but a component has not reached its minimum (less than 40% for theoretical/reports or less than 3/10 for practicals), the final grade will be capped at 4 points. Students who passed practicals or coursework in the same academic year with a grade of 5 or higher can validate those components.
